quote: **IN-5 Duplicate check.** The reconciliation job reports every number that appears twice in the shared sequence of all regions. / **IN-4 Gap check.** The nightly reconciliation job reports every gap in the invoice sequence to the finance team.

**RF-4 Refund method.** Money goes back to the payment method that was used for the order; the customer may ask for store credit in its place. / **RF-3 Refund obligation.** A customer who cancels an order or returns an item within the allowed window is refunded the full price paid for it, including shipping when the whole order is cancelled.
**BK-3 Storage platform.** Copies of the data are managed by the storage platform.

**RL-5 Excess requests.** Requests above the limit are rejected with HTTP 429 and a `Retry-After` header. The server then repeats the rejected request on the client's behalf, as described in RL-2. / **RL-4 Limit.** Each API key may send at most 100 requests per minute.
**NO-2 Opt-out.** A customer who opts out of marketing notifications receives none of them, on any channel, from the moment the preference is saved.
The worker retries a failed delivery up to 8 times with exponential backoff and marks it `FAILED` after the ninth failed attempt.

**RF-4 Refund method.** Refunds return to the original payment method. Store credit is issued only when the customer chooses it. / **RF-3 Refund obligation.** A customer who cancels an order or returns an item within the allowed window is refunded the full price paid for it, including shipping when the whole order is cancelled.
A failed delivery is retried by the worker up to 8 times with exponential backoff, and it is marked `FAILED` after the ninth failed attempt.

**PR-4 Link lifetime.** A password reset link stays valid until it is used or until the customer asks for a newer link. / **PR-3 One-time use.** A password reset link can be used once. After a successful reset the link stops working.
